response.message: We're building an AWS incident explainer: it collects synthetic logs and traces, redacts them before storage, searches them, and has a Bedrock-backed runtime give operators an answer that cites trace and log IDs. Log text is treated as untrusted data, not instructions. I've drawn the full end-to-end flow. Only the Bedrock model connection has a typed generator; collection, redaction, search and the analysis code still need engineering. For a first local test, we can replay a small synthetic incident through the redaction and analysis code with a scripted model reply. That checks the plumbing, redaction and citation format, and whether planted 'ignore your instructions' log lines get through. It says nothing about how well a model reasons. That needs a separate run against a real Bedrock model in an approved account and region, and we haven't verified either yet. Which details must redaction remove before anything is stored, for example emails, IP addresses, user IDs or tokens?

proposal.title: AWS log/trace incident explainer – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic services → ADOT collection → Lambda redaction → S3 evidence and OpenSearch search, plus X-Ray traces → Lambda analysis runtime using Bedrock and Bedrock Guardrails → IAM-authenticated API for the operator. Assumptions: the account, region, model ID and access are not yet selected or verified. Only the Bedrock binding is typed. All other wires need engineering. Nothing has been deployed.

data.label: Synthetic services
data.description: Existing synthetic workload emitting logs and OpenTelemetry traces. Outside provisioning scope.

data.label: ADOT Collector
data.description: Receives OTLP logs and traces. Sends traces to X-Ray and logs to Firehose.

data.label: Trace store
data.description: Stores distributed traces. Attributes are redacted at the collector before export.

data.label: Log delivery stream
data.description: Buffers log records and calls the redaction transform before delivery.

data.label: Redaction transform
data.description: Applies the rule-based redaction rules (still to be confirmed) and tags records as untrusted text. Owns its role and logs.

data.label: Redacted evidence archive
data.description: Private, encrypted, versioned store for redacted log batches. This is the evidence of record.

data.label: Log search index
data.description: Searchable index of redacted logs, keyed by trace ID and record ID.

data.label: Incident analysis runtime
data.description: Correlates X-Ray traces with OpenSearch hits for an incident window. Sends the evidence to the model as quoted data and returns an explanation that cites trace and record IDs, or abstains. This application code is not yet generated.

data.label: Prompt/answer guardrail
data.description: Filters prompt attacks and sensitive information in model input and output. The configuration still needs to be defined.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Direct foundation model through Converse. The model ID, access, region and quotas are unverified.

data.label: Operator API
data.description: IAM-authenticated HTTP API for incident questions. No anonymous access.

data.label: On-call operator
data.description: Existing operator identity. Outside provisioning scope.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If unredacted data reaches the index or prompts, secrets or personal data can leak into answers and long-lived storage.
requirementDrafts.basis: User asked to 'Include collection, redaction, storage/search'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: sensitive fields are redacted from logs and trace attributes before they reach storage, search or the model.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Logs can contain attacker-controlled strings. Without this rule, they could inject prompts that mislead operators.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: log and trace content is passed to the model only as quoted evidence. Instructions found inside log text must never change the runtime's tools, scope or output policy.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Operators must be able to check the conclusion. An answer without evidence could send an incident response in the wrong direction.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: 'an operator-facing answer with source evidence'; REQ-001.
requirementDrafts.statement: Every incident explanation cites the trace IDs and log record IDs it relies on. It abstains when the evidence is insufficient.

Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message: The emulation report shows no failed checks, and the flow is still whole: nothing was dropped to get a pass. It is blocked by 8 gaps. Seven of them are missing native code for the collector, X-Ray, Firehose, redaction, OpenSearch and the analysis runtime, plus an import plan for the existing synthetic services. That is product engineering work, and changing the diagram won't fix it. The one gap we can fix ourselves is the first: the redacted evidence archive (Amazon S3) has no rule for who may access it. Right now only Firehose writes to it. I don't want to add a reader that our requirements don't support. Who should read the archive? For example: only the on-call operator, with read-only access to check citations, or the analysis runtime, or nobody except Firehose writing to it, kept as an audit record.
